entries.body: With several searches running, one still being answered could be cleared away, so it said 'The search stopped arriving' and the answer was missing when you came back. Running searches are kept until their answer is saved, a retried search keeps its place and colour, and a search from one article no longer lands in another after you switch.

entries.title: Two sign-in mix-ups are fixed
entries.body: Just after signing in from an emailed link, you could be sent on as if you had not signed in; that no longer happens. And a failed sign-in could hold on to the page you were heading for, so your next sign-in took you there; a failed sign-in now forgets it.

entries.title: Retry after Start again sends one request
entries.body: On the Metadata page, pressing Retry after Start again had failed could close back onto the old failure, and pressing twice sent two retries. Retry shows it is starting straight away and sends one.

entries.title: Profile and Metadata boxes save as you type
entries.body: The About you box on your profile and the box on an article's Metadata page for why you are reading it save after two seconds without typing, as well as when you click away. Each shows whether it has saved, warns before you leave with words unsaved, and tries to save if you switch tab or close the page.

entries.title: Dictation warns you when the microphone is silent
entries.body: If the microphone stays silent while you are dictating, the dictation strip turns a warm colour, shows a warning sign and plays a soft chime, once per dictation. Once you have sent a report, the Feedback dialog no longer shows the old recording's error each time you reopen it.

entries.title: Annotations no longer cut section titles short
entries.body: At the top of the Annotations column, the part and section you are in wrap onto up to two lines each instead of being cut short; point at, tap or tab to one to read it whole. In a window too narrow for both, pressing Annotations closes the panel beside the article and shows your notes.

entries.title: Clicking a Diagram picture enlarges it
entries.body: In Diagram, clicking an Illustrated picture or the background of a Sketch opens it enlarged, as the Enlarge button does, and a double-click leaves it open. Quotes and Citations give up a row at the top of their panels, which leaves more room on a phone held sideways; Citations' explanations sit behind a small (i) icon.

entries.title: Clearer labels in Glossary, Remember and your library
entries.body: In the Glossary panel, a looked-up term says whether its definition came from a web search or from the AI's own knowledge, replacing the old 'checked' labels. Pointing at Remember's Reply menu, at Topics above your library or at its coloured topic bars explains what they mean. An article's Metadata page puts its AI processing in one section.

entries.title: Simple summaries share one reading of the article
entries.body: When you ask for the Simple summaries of an article, the fullest level starts first and the shorter ones begin once it is under way, so they all reuse the AI's reading of the article. That makes them cheaper to produce. Very short articles still start them all together.

entries.title: A working microphone is no longer reported missing
entries.body: With some microphones, such as AirPods on an iPhone, every dictation warned that the chosen microphone was unavailable even though it was working. Dictation recognises the same microphone by its name, and when it really has changed, it says, where it can, which one you chose and which it is using.

entries.title: Remember keeps one conversation per article
entries.body: Remember is a single conversation for each article rather than a list, and its conversations no longer appear in Chat's list. If you had more than one, their messages have been moved into your earliest. A Start over button clears it once the last answer has finished, and on a short screen the box you type in takes no more than 30% of the screen's height, so the conversation stays in view.

entries.title: Every mode panel has an information button
entries.body: The panel beside the article has an (i) button in its top-right corner in every mode except Referee, which keeps its own how-it-works control. It explains what the mode does and how, and where it can, adds counts, caveats and how the panel's contents were made. Descriptions that used to sit at the top and bottom of several panels have moved in there, so they no longer crowd the panel.

entries.title: Links to passages you can see are highlighted
entries.body: When a mode's panel and the article are side by side, any link in the panel to a passage currently on your screen is highlighted, and the highlights follow as you scroll. In Trajectory, the prompt for the current row comes before the quote it refers to.

entries.title: Citations drops a repeated line and flashes clearer
entries.body: In the Citations panel, a work whose title already gives the author and year no longer repeats them on a line beneath; point at the title, or tap it on a touchscreen, to see the full reference. Jumping to where a work is first cited marks the cited words with a stronger highlight and a pulse, lasting 2.4 seconds.

entries.title: Signing in has a page of its own
entries.body: Signing in and creating an account happen on their own page, with a switch between the two, Google and email both offered from the start, and a Show/Hide button for your password. The home page and the pricing page link there instead of carrying the form at the bottom.

entries.title: Annotations is renamed Marginalia
entries.body: The notes column beside the article, behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page, is called Marginalia. Old links to it still work.

entries.title: More hover labels, quieter Experimental button
entries.body: The line down the side of the article that shows where you have spent reading time shows its label when you point at it; before, the label never appeared. Question notes in Marginalia show a short explanation on hover, and the Experimental button no longer turns orange as if selected.

entries.title: PDF author lists no longer lose names
entries.body: When you added a PDF, a list of several authors could be stored as a single name, and bylines with each author's institution and email address set beneath their name were not accepted. Both are fixed: every word after the last author is checked, and those bylines are read.

entries.title: Free accounts can receive extra articles as a gift
entries.body: We can give a reader extra articles on the Free plan as a gift, tied to their email address; it takes effect the next time they are signed in with that address confirmed. If you are on the Free plan, or your subscription has lapsed, your library has a new box under Add article showing how many more private articles you have room for, any gifts you hold, and a notice you can dismiss when one arrives. The plan wording on Pricing and your profile counts gifts too.

entries.title: Order buttons stay on one line on touch screens
entries.body: On a phone or tablet, the buttons that change the order in Quotes, Citations, Glossary, Debate and FAQ sit on a single line you can swipe sideways, with the count kept in place. The order you chose is always scrolled into view, so the panel takes less height without hiding which order is active.

links.label: Quotes, Glossary and the other modes

entries.title: Chat and Sketch panels open where they should
entries.body: An empty Chat or Remember conversation could open scrolled past its opening hint, especially on a phone held sideways; it opens at the top. Switching the floating chat window to another conversation no longer carries over the last one's scroll position or half-typed message. On wide screens, full-screen Sketch leaves a margin you can click to close it.

entries.title: Dig deeper searches the web, then answers
entries.body: In the Glossary panel and on an answered comment, the old web-search buttons are now one action, Dig deeper. It always searches the web, then a more capable AI answers from what it found, replacing the first answer; it takes longer. Before, the search could be skipped and an answer given from memory under a web-search label. A glossary term that already has an answer now offers Dig deeper again beneath it.

entries.title: Plain-words summaries use the more capable AI
entries.body: The plain-words levels in Summary are now written by the more capable AI for every article, whether or not its High-powered AI switch is on. In our tests it was less likely to swap the article's own contrasting terms for looser ones. Each summary is still checked against the original text.

entries.title: A gift of free articles arrives by email
entries.body: When someone is given extra free articles, an email now goes to their address telling them about the gift. The privacy policy now says so, because this can be the first email sent to an address that never gave it to us.

entries.title: Add several PDF or HTML files at once
entries.body: Choose or drop two or more PDF or HTML files and they are added together, with a panel to stop the batch or retry a single file. Files already in your library are skipped, and if you reach your allowance the rest of the batch stops. Each one arrives marked Not AI-processed yet, with its title, authors, abstract and DOI, and for a PDF the file itself. Nothing more is done with it until you press Read this.

entries.title: Structure can show the whole outline at once
entries.body: Structure mode has a second view, Expanded, beside the usual Fisheye: every part and section at any depth, each with its summary, in one scrolling list that moves with you when you read into another section. The arrow keys also behave the same everywhere: Up and Down step one paragraph at a time, except over the strip showing where you are in the article, and with Structure open, Left and Right step between the smallest sections.

entries.title: Investigate in Citations is renamed Dig deeper
entries.body: In Citations, the button beside each cited work is renamed Dig deeper. Every press searches the web first, which you see as it happens, and the answer comes from a stronger AI with more room before it is cut off. Results from the old Investigate button no longer show; press Dig deeper for a fresh one.

entries.title: Summary keeps to its three levels
entries.body: Summary mode drops its outline of parts and sections, which repeated Structure, and keeps the Brief, Simple and Fuller summaries, with a button at each end of the slider, in a slightly wider panel. Newly made summaries and Tweets threads leave out authors, funding, acknowledgements and similar paperwork unless the piece uses them, and end on its conclusion.

entries.title: Trajectory is renamed Skim, among smaller changes
entries.body: Trajectory is called Skim, and old links still open it; its stop cards no longer show FAQ questions. Chat is told which passages were on your screen when you asked. Sketch's wait message says about a minute. Glossary terms have a heavier dotted underline than cross-references, and the reading-time line in the margin explains itself when you point at it.

entries.title: Past imports show more; Metadata page has search
entries.body: On the add page, past imports show their source and time, and a failed one has a Report this button. The box for why you are reading shows whether it saved; leave it empty and the article asks once when it opens. On the Metadata page, contents open the section you pick and a search finds sections by topic.

entries.title: Fewer gaps and failures adding PDFs and books
entries.body: A PDF's tables could show only a caption over an empty box, and figures made of several panels could be missing; both appear, for PDFs added from now on. Long documents such as books could fail while building their levels of detail; small faults are repaired where possible, or the AI is asked once more.

entries.title: Dictation follows your computer's microphone setting
entries.body: In Chrome and browsers built on it, dictation and Live conversation with no microphone picked could listen to the browser's own default instead of the one your computer uses, and hear nothing. They follow your computer's setting, the dictation strip names the microphone in use while dictation is on, and the first choice in the list is called System default.

entries.title: Summary starts writing itself when you open it
entries.body: Pressing Summary on one of your articles that has no summary yet starts writing one, instead of leaving an empty panel, and the panel no longer says nobody has asked while one is being written. Summary is also among the main modes you can choose to have prepared when you add an article.

entries.title: Archive button at the top of the article
entries.body: On your own articles, an Archive button sits at the top of the reading page beside the sharing mark, and Put back undoes it. It stays in step with the same control on the article's Metadata page.

entries.title: Your plan and any gifts are explained
entries.body: Your profile page and the allowance box in your library show your plan, any gifts you received, and how it works, such as when limits reset. If someone gives you a gift and you have an account, the email can show your allowance before and after it, and may carry a note from the giver. The privacy policy says so.

entries.title: Experimental: the margin gathers notes from other modes
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on your profile page, the Marginalia column to the right of the article also shows FAQ answers, Debate sources, citations and your comments, one line each beside the passage they belong to, opening in place. Opening the column starts no new AI work.

entries.title: Experimental: a new typeface for the AI's words
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on your profile page, text the AI wrote appears in IBM Plex Mono instead of Courier Prime. The author's words, the AI's and your own each keep their own typeface in more places, including Tweets, Quotes, Sketch, hover cards, chat and search, while the app's own labels stay in its usual type.

entries.title: More Dig deeper presses each day in Citations
entries.body: The daily limit on Dig deeper in Citations, shared by all readers together, went from 25 to 62. Your own limit of 20 a day is unchanged, so you should meet the daily-limit message less often on a busy day.

entries.title: The reading page no longer scrolls sideways
entries.body: On a Mac set to always show scrollbars, every article could scroll a little sideways, because the page counted the scrollbar as room to fill. It fits the window now. On very wide windows, the panel beside the article also uses the spare room.

entries.title: Metadata page contents list shows on an iPad
entries.body: The contents list in the left margin of an article's Metadata page was hidden on medium-width windows, such as an iPad held sideways. It shows there now, and the page moves over just enough to make room for it.

entries.title: Help page, and more in the command bar
entries.body: A Help page explains each mode, when to use which, your library and your account, with a search and answers to common questions. Open it from the footer, the Help button beside the mode buttons, or the command bar, which takes you to the part about the mode you are in; each mode's (i) card links there too. On your own articles, the command bar can also run a mode again, archive the article, open its sharing settings or download a copy.

entries.title: A quick search beside words and meaning
entries.body: Search has a third option beside words and meaning: quick. The AI scores every paragraph of the article against your question and gives back the whole paragraphs that fit, kept with your other searches. When a quick search has finished, its flesh out button runs the full meaning search.

entries.title: Hide glossary terms, or add looked-up ones
entries.body: You can hide a glossary term: it leaves the text and waits under Hidden in the Glossary panel. A term you look up can join your glossary, kept out of what you share. Underlined terms' cards offer Dig deeper, and a term written with a hyphen also matches it written with a space, in glossaries already made too.

entries.title: Summary opens on Brief; sentences point to passages
entries.body: Summary opens on its Brief level unless you choose another. In newly written summaries, a sentence can be linked to the passage it rests on: point at it to see that passage, or follow it there. Older summaries read as before.

entries.title: Include other readers' shared articles in your library
entries.body: An Include public button shows articles other readers have shared, in a section below your own. Under a search, buttons offer to include archived or public articles, with a count of matches where one can be given. In the topics' More detail view, pointing at an article shows a card with a short description, its dates and its topics.

entries.title: Edit your profile from the badge, then regenerate
entries.body: The 'written for your profile' badge opens your purpose and profile for editing in place, saved as you type. If you change them after a mode was written, Regenerate rewrites it for you in Summary, Glossary, Ideas, Tweets, Sketch and Quiz; regenerating a quiz clears your answers so far.

entries.title: Fold sections; press a mode again to close
entries.body: Headings with text beneath them have an arrow that folds their section away; Alt-click folds or opens them all. Pressing the open mode's button again closes it, and Plain closes Marginalia as well. Each Marginalia note says which mode made it and who wrote it, and FAQ, Debate and Ideas notes appear when they finish, without reopening it.

entries.title: Source notices on shared articles, and feedback emails
entries.body: Anyone reading an article you have shared sees, at the top, where it came from, how to ask for it to be taken down, and that the AI services used do not train on it. Separately, if feedback you sent leads to a change, we may email you once it is live; that email does not quote what you wrote.

entries.title: A Quick search box in the bottom bar
entries.body: On your own articles, the bar along the bottom of the page has a Quick search box: type, pause, and Search opens with the passages that match. Press / to jump to it, Enter to search at once, Escape to clear it; on a touch screen, in a narrow window or when space runs short it is a lightning-bolt button instead. Separately, quick search in the Search panel runs whenever you pause after three or more characters, keeping one saved search per burst of typing rather than one per pause.

entries.title: Remember gains a Tutorial; Recall adapts to you
entries.body: Remember has three parts: Recall, Tutorial and Quiz. Tutorial is new: it aims to teach a little of the article each turn, set you one task (say it back, apply it, or push back), and return to earlier points every three or four turns. Recall drops its four reply styles for one approach that aims to keep replies short, answer direct questions, and fill in a gap when you are stuck rather than make you fail twice.

entries.title: Bookmarks stand out, and comments need no AI
entries.body: A bookmarked paragraph gets a filled, full-strength mark beside it, and bookmarking opens a comment box unless you have moved on; closing it keeps the bookmark. The box says the AI does not reply, so a comment can be just yours. Comments are labelled Bookmark, Comment, Comment + AI or Question, and your passage questions appear in the margin notes.

entries.title: Quotes mark the strip; headings stay in view
entries.body: The lines Quotes picks out show as green marks on the strip showing where you are in the article, in every mode. Point at one in the text for its card, with previous and next; Quotes mode adds large step buttons and arrow keys. With Experimental features on, the headings you are under stay at the top as you read.

entries.title: Easier tapping on library cards and close crosses
entries.body: Library cards keep their actions on the bottom row; on a touch screen, wide cards show large action icons instead of a menu, and narrow ones a clearer menu button. The close crosses on dialogs and panels now share one size, with a bigger tap area on touch screens. The panel's scrollbar is easier to see, where the browser allows.

entries.title: Brief summaries aim for plainer words
entries.body: New Brief summaries are told to use everyday words even if your profile says expert: at most two technical terms, each explained. Every level aims to start with what the piece is after and what kind of piece it is. Older summaries are marked out of date, not redone. A cancelled drag on the level slider still asks for the new level.

entries.title: Citations sort by date; Debate seeks citing work
entries.body: Citations can be ordered by date: oldest first, by the year each work shows, undated works last, offered when at least one work has a year. New Debate searches ask for work that cites and discusses the article, scholarly work included, and check more than the first passage they find on a page.

entries.title: Feedback you send is also emailed to us
entries.body: When you send feedback, a plain-text copy may also be emailed to our own inbox, with what you wrote, the page address and your email address. The privacy policy says so. Sending the same report twice does not send a second email.

entries.title: You can steer the Illustrated picture
entries.body: Illustrated mode has a box asking "How should it come out?", where you can say in your own words, typed or dictated, up to 400 characters, what you want from the picture. Your note is passed to the AI that plans the painting, and a Paint again button sits beside an existing picture so you can try another direction. Pictures already painted stay as they are.

entries.title: High-powered AI can be switched on while adding
entries.body: The page for adding an article has a second tick box, High-powered AI, beside the one for generating the main modes. Before, you could only switch it on from the article's Metadata page once it had been added. It is off by default and is not remembered from one article to the next.

entries.title: Live conversation shows what it is doing
entries.body: Talking to the article out loud shows one status (Connecting, Listening, Thinking, Speaking) and a sound-level meter from the moment the microphone opens. What is said appears once, at the end of the chat. A failure gives the reason and a Try again button; the microphone settings sit under Advanced, and the dictation button there is gone.

entries.title: Structure is told not to summarise the abstract
entries.body: When Structure outlines a newly added article, it is told to treat the title block, the abstract and the reference list as parts that only identify the piece: a short plain label, no summary, no question. The abstract is already the author's own summary. Summary and the Tweets thread are told the same about the title block and the reference list, though not the abstract; outlines already built are unchanged.

entries.title: Feedback filters show how many reports each holds
entries.body: In the Feedback dialog's Earlier tab, the All, Shipped and Not shipped filters each show how many of your reports they hold, and screen readers read the number properly. When a list is cut short, it says how many it is showing out of how many there are.

entries.title: The where-you-are marker scrolls with less redrawing
entries.body: The marker on the strip showing where you are in the article moves in a way that asks the browser to redraw much less as you scroll, in our tests in a desktop browser. It sits exactly where it did before.

entries.title: Opened margin notes are no longer cut off
entries.body: Opening a note in the margin beside the article showed its answer but left its question, title or headline cut off with an ellipsis; it wraps onto as many lines as it needs. A passage you asked about in chat is also shown there in the article's own typeface, since those are the author's words.

entries.title: Tag your articles, privately, and filter by them
entries.body: You can give articles your own tags, from the Tag button on each card or row in your library, or the tag box near the top of an article's Metadata page. Only you see them. Once you have tags, a Tags row appears above Topics; pick several tags and topics and your library narrows to the articles that match them all. Exports include an article's tags.

entries.title: Highlight passages in four colours
entries.body: When you select words to comment on, you can give them a yellow, green, blue or pink highlight, and change the colour later from the comment. A highlight with no note, and the AI not asked, is kept as a plain highlight: it shows in the text and in your list of comments, with no note in the margin. Where highlights overlap, the newest one sets the colour and is the one a click opens.

entries.title: Modes are told to skip an article's paperwork
entries.body: The AI behind Sketch, Illustrated, FAQ, Quiz, Ideas, Quotes, Glossary, Timeline and Debate is now told to pass over passages that only say what the piece is, or how it was produced, published and sourced. Evidence, reasoning, method and limitations still count. Results you already have mostly change only when they are made again.

entries.title: Paragraph icons move to the text's right
entries.body: The small icons beside each paragraph and heading (link, comment, ? and …) and the reading-time line now sit to the right of the article rather than the left. On wide screens the icons and the article's title also line up more closely with the text, where they had drifted out of line.

entries.title: Where a section sits, and how much you've read
entries.body: Point at or tap a section on the strip showing where you are, and its card shows where it sits in the article's outline: its part, the sections around it, and its own sub-sections. In Quiz, the share of the piece you have read is drawn as a small pie; point at or tap it for the figure.

entries.title: The Glossary button moves to the panel's top
entries.body: The button that finds terms is the first thing in the Glossary panel, and says Find more when it will add to your list, or Find terms again when it will replace it. On an article's Metadata page, pressing Metadata again (or Cmd/Ctrl-Enter) takes you back to the article; it used to do nothing.

entries.title: Tap to talk when a conversation stalls
entries.body: When you talk to an article out loud, background voices can keep it waiting for you to finish speaking. The notice that appears then offers Tap to talk: press Talk, speak, press Done, and the reply follows. It stays on for the rest of that call, Reconnect included; hands-free calls are otherwise unchanged.

entries.title: Cards open with a tap on touch screens
entries.body: On a phone or tablet, the cards in Structure and on the reading-time line beside each paragraph did not open at all. A tap opens them now; in Structure a second tap takes you there, and rows without a card still go straight there. Citations cards opened by a tap close when you scroll.

entries.title: Choose a light or dark appearance
entries.body: Your profile page has a new Appearance setting with three choices: Light, Dark and System, which follows your device. It applies across the whole app, and it is remembered on each device separately. Until you choose, the app stays dark, so nothing changes unless you want it to.

entries.title: Look up an article's authors
entries.body: Point at an author's name at the top of an article and the card that appears has a "Find out more" line, with a Google Scholar search for that author and a web search for their name and affiliation. Each opens in a new tab. The same links sit beside each author on the article's Metadata page, which is where to find them on a phone.

entries.title: Earlier feedback shows the page it came from
entries.body: In the feedback dialog, each report on the Earlier tab says which page you sent it from. Only the page is shown, never anything you searched for, so you can tell your reports apart at a glance.

entries.title: The tag box is easier to use
entries.body: The box for adding a tag, in your library and on an article's Metadata page, is announced as "Add a tag" to screen readers, and phone keyboards that support it show a Done key. Pressing Enter still adds the tag and leaves the box open for the next one.

entries.title: Help no longer calls the typefaces experimental
entries.body: The Help page still described giving each voice its own typeface as an experiment, although it is on for every reader. Help now says so plainly, and the item is gone from its list of experimental features.
